_comment: Vendor cgroup layout for Android 17.
The stock /system/etc/cgroups.json mounts cpu and cpuset on cgroup v1
paths (/dev/cpuctl, /dev/cpuset). Mounting a v1 hierarchy calls
rebind_subsystems(), which *removes* those controllers from the v2
default hierarchy (cgroup.c: cgrp_dfl_root.subsys_mask &=
~dfl_disable_ss_mask). That is why cgroup.controllers only ever listed
memory and pids here even though both cpuset and cpu had dfl_cftypes.
So: keep blkio on v1 (legacy block throttling userspace still wants
it), and do not re-request cpu or cpuset for v1, leaving both attached
to v2 where the A17 framework expects them. The v2 Controllers list
below is what actually gets activated under /sys/fs/cgroup.
CORRECTION: an earlier version of this comment claimed /dev/cpuset was
still mounted by init so that the MediaTeK scripts in
init.mt6893.power.rc kept working. That was wrong, and the scripts were
silently failing: nothing mounts /dev/cpuset any more, because the Cgroups
(v1) list below deliberately does not request it. The cpuset writes in
that rc file have since been removed. Per-state CPU masks are applied on
v2 instead, by libprocessgroup writing each task's existing
/apps|system/uid_N/pid_M/cpuset.cpus leaf (see etc/task_profiles.json).
Do not re-add /dev/cpuset writes, and do not re-request cpuset under
Cgroups: mounting it on v1 would call rebind_subsystems() and pull it
back out of the v2 hierarchy again.
NeedsActivation is what makes libprocessgroup write "+cpuset" to
each cgroup's cgroup.subtree_control, and MaxActivationDepth 3
reaches root -> apps -> apps/uid_N. createProcessGroupInternal()
calls ActivateControllers() every time it makes a per-uid group,
so the controllers land on groups that do not exist yet at boot.
This has to be done from userspace: the kernel does not propagate
a parent's subtree_control to a child made with mkdir, and
enabling cpuset only at the root leaves apps/uid_N without the
cpuset control files, so no task can be placed there.
